svg.title: One shared population type changes the distribution of a count
svg.desc: Type A is normal with mean one hundred and variance two hundred twenty-five; type B has mean one hundred twenty and variance one hundred. Their selection weights are zero point six and zero point four. Exceeding one hundred fifteen has component probabilities approximately zero point one five eight six five five two five three nine and zero point six nine one four six two four six one three. Their weighted one-reading probability is approximately zero point three seven one seven seven eight one three six nine. The upper plot shows the component normal densities and their shaded upper tails; it does not replace them with a normal model obtained by averaging parameters. For four independent trials, each with a fresh type choice and an independent measurement, the count has a binomial distribution with the weighted success probability. For one type chosen for the group, four readings are independent conditional on that type; their count distribution is the weighted mixture of the two conditional binomial laws. The lower plot compares the full count probability masses. The probability of at least one exceedance rounds to 0.8442 for fresh choices and 0.6957 for a shared choice. Both expected counts round to one point four eight seven one. Equal one-reading probabilities and equal expectations do not imply the same group-event probabilities.
